title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore Auditorium on 1967-05-05
source: Don Wolfe's 3.75 ips > Akai GX636 direct tape head output  > Bottlehead tube tape pre pair Tesla tubes circa 1980  > Apogee Mini Me 24/96  > Apogee Mini DAC monitoring and mastering  > FLAC

ai_review.summary: A good‑quality soundboard recording with corrected pitch and reduced noise that captures a free, loose performance beloved by fans despite weak vocals.
ai_review.review: The release improves on the Ben Yerys tape by putting tracks in the proper order, applying less aggressive noise reduction and fixing pitch issues, resulting in a solid soundboard sound. Musically it’s an early‑era favorite – the band plays free and loose with high energy, and listeners note an early Jerry Gibson guitar appearance even though the singing is described as horrible.

ai_rating.rationale: Strong fan enthusiasm for the performance (two 5‑star reviews) and clear technical improvements give a high show score, while one very low rating points to lingering recording concerns, balancing to an overall ~4‑star rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Tracks now in correct order, less aggressive noise reduction, pitch corrected on several songs; still based on the same source as older releases.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Possibly the earliest surviving recording of Jerry playing a Gibson; noted for free, loose guitar work.
